title: Euler tour + subtree/path queries (BIT/segtree)
relevance: Medium — org-chart / file-tree “sum or update this department” maps directly to flatten+BIT; full path/LCA variants are rarer in OAs but dominate CF Div2 D–E tree DS. Striver never teaches tree linearization, so this is a pure CP unlock.
company_notes: Org/manager trees: sum salaries under manager X or add bonus to department X → Subtree Queries / Ki (flatten + Fenwick). File-system / nested folders: toggle or recolor a folder and all descendants → Euler range update (Danil / New Year Tree shape, often simplified). Path cost after edge edits: update road length, query distance between cities → ABC294 G / CSES Path Queries + LCA (Juspay-style). Hierarchy reachability: is A an ancestor of B? / any of these IDs under boss X? → tin/tout checks (Tree Queries / Unusual Entertainment).

phases.goal: Map org-chart, folder, path-distance, and hierarchy wording to Euler flatten + Fenwick/segtree (vs needing LCA or HLD).

must_hit.point: Signal words: subtree sum/add/flip after updates, values on root→node path, “descendants at depth h”, color assign on a whole subtree, company hierarchy queries.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists those signals and reaches for Euler tour + BIT/segtree rather than plain DFS only.

must_hit.point: Org/manager “sum salaries under manager X” or “add bonus to department X” → Subtree Queries / Ki (flatten + Fenwick).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maps department sum/add under a manager to flatten + Fenwick subtree range ops.

must_hit.point: File-system toggle/recolor of a folder and descendants → Euler range update; “update road length, query distance between cities” → ABC294 G / CSES Path Queries + LCA; “is A an ancestor of B?” / IDs under boss X → tin/tout checks.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Splits folder recolor, edge-edit distances, and ancestor/reachability into the matching Euler shapes.

must_hit.point: Full path/LCA variants are rarer in OAs but dominate CF Div2 D–E tree DS; Striver never teaches tree linearization.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Notes OA rarity of full path/LCA variants versus CF Div2 D–E dominance and the Striver gap.

probes: What wording makes you flatten the tree with tin/tout instead of walking the subtree each query?
Is this a department sum/add, a folder recolor, a city-distance after edge edits, or an ancestor check?

hints.1: Ask whether the ask is under-a-node aggregates, root→node values, folder-wide flips, or ancestor/reachability.
hints.2: Manager sum/bonus → Subtree Queries/Ki; folder recolor → Euler range update; road update + city distance → Path Queries/ABC294 G + LCA; ancestor/under-boss → tin/tout.
hints.3: Say: signals are subtree sum/add/flip, root→node values, descendants at depth h, subtree color assign, hierarchy queries; org sum/bonus → flatten+Fenwick; folder toggle → Euler range update; edge edit + distance → Path Queries/ABC294 G + LCA; ancestor/IDs under boss → tin/tout; path/LCA variants rarer in OAs, big on CF Div2 D–E.

phases.goal: State DFS tin/tout flatten so subtree→range and root→node→prefix, then when to add LCA.

must_hit.point: Root the tree and DFS-timestamp each node: enter → tin[v], leave → tout[v]; subtree of v is contiguous [tin[v], tout[v]] (or [tin[v], tin[v]+sz[v]-1]).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Defines tin/tout in one DFS and the contiguous subtree index range.

must_hit.point: Put a Fenwick/segtree on that linear order so subtree ops become range ops.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States that the tour array + Fenwick/segtree turns subtree asks into range asks.

must_hit.point: Root→node path ops become prefix ops via the +x at tin, −x at tout+1 difference trick.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names the tour difference endpoints and prefix-to-tin answer for root→node.

must_hit.point: Ancestor tests are tin[u] ≤ tin[v] ≤ tout[u]; combine with LCA for arbitrary u–v paths.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives the tin/tout ancestor check and says LCA is needed for general u–v paths.

probes: How do you turn a subtree query into an array range query?
How do root→node path sums become prefix sums on the tour?

hints.1: Timestamp enter/leave in DFS, then think contiguous indices under a node.
hints.2: Subtree → range on [tin,tout]; root→node → prefix via +x at tin and −x at tout+1; ancestors via tin/tout; general paths need LCA.
hints.3: Say: tin on enter, tout on leave; subtree = [tin[v],tout[v]] (or tin..tin+sz-1); Fenwick/segtree on the tour; root→node via +x at tin, −x at tout+1 then prefix to tin[u]; ancestor if tin[u]≤tin[v]≤tout[u]; arbitrary u–v needs LCA.

phases.goal: Code tin/tout DFS, subtree PURS, path-to-root BIT-as-diff, LCA path formula, and lazy/offline variants.

must_hit.point: Write tin/tout (or in/out) in one DFS; subtree of v = contiguous [tin[v], tout[v]]; sz[v] = tout[v] − tin[v] (convention-dependent — pick one and stick to it).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Codes one DFS for timestamps and states the sz ↔ tout−tin link under a fixed convention.

must_hit.point: Subtree PURS: store value at tin[v]; point update tin[v]; query sum/min/OR on [tin[v], tout[v]] with Fenwick or segtree.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Places the value at tin[v] and does point-update + range query on the subtree interval.

must_hit.point: Path root→u: on value change of v by δ, range-add [tin[v], tout[v]] by δ (BIT-as-diff: +δ at tin[v], −δ at tout[v]+1); answer = prefix sum to tin[u].
must_hit.evidence_hint: Writes the two BIT endpoints and answers with prefix to tin[u].

must_hit.point: Path u–v: path(u)+path(v)−2·path(lca) (edge weights) or adjust by ±value[lca] for node weights; need LCA template.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States the edge-weight path identity and the node-weight LCA adjustment.

must_hit.point: Subtree assign/flip → lazy segtree on the tour array; offline distinct-in-subtree: scan Euler order, keep only last index of each color in a BIT (Distinct Colors).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names lazy-on-tour for assign/flip and last-occurrence BIT for offline distinct colors.

probes: Where do you store a node’s value for subtree sum queries?
Walk me through updating a node so root→u path sums stay correct.
How do you get an arbitrary u–v path from root→node prefixes?

hints.1: One DFS for tin/tout; decide whether the op is subtree range, root→node prefix, or full u–v.
hints.2: PURS: value at tin, query [tin,tout]; path-to-root: +δ at tin, −δ at tout+1, prefix to tin[u]; u–v via LCA formula; assign/flip → lazy; distinct → last-occurrence BIT.
hints.3: Say: tin/tout in one DFS, sz=tout−tin under one convention; store at tin[v], point-update, range on [tin,tout]; root→u via +δ at tin[v], −δ at tout[v]+1, prefix to tin[u]; path(u)+path(v)−2·path(lca) (edges) or ±value[lca] (nodes); lazy for assign/flip; Distinct Colors last-occurrence BIT.

phases.goal: State the O(1) ancestor check and where Euler’s range reduction stops (need HLD).

must_hit.point: Ancestor test in O(1): tin[u] ≤ tin[v] && tout[v] ≤ tout[u] (equivalently tin[u] ≤ tin[v] ≤ tout[u] with matching tout convention).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Quotes the O(1) tin/tout ancestor predicate and notes the convention pair.

must_hit.point: After flatten, subtree ops are contiguous range ops and root→node ops are prefix ops on the tour (via the difference trick).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States the structural reduction: subtree→range, root→node→prefix.

must_hit.point: Euler shines for subtrees and root-paths; arbitrary path aggregates with updates usually need HLD (Path Queries II).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Draws the capability limit and names Path Queries II / HLD as the upgrade.

must_hit.point: New Year Tree stretch: ≤60 colors → uint64 OR on tour ranges.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cites the ≤60 → uint64 bitmask capacity on Euler ranges.

probes: How fast is an ancestor check after tin/tout?
When does Euler stop being enough and you need HLD?

hints.1: Ancestor is a constant-time timestamp compare; capability differs for subtree vs arbitrary path.
hints.2: O(1) tin/tout ancestor; subtree→range and root→node→prefix; arbitrary path aggregates with updates → HLD / Path Queries II.
hints.3: Say: ancestor in O(1) via tin/tout inequalities; flatten makes subtree a range and root→node a prefix; Euler for subtrees/root-paths, HLD (Path Queries II) for arbitrary path aggregates with updates; ≤60 colors → uint64 OR on tour ranges.

phases.goal: Catch tin/tout convention bugs, wrong path formulas, and using Euler when HLD is required.

must_hit.point: sz[v] = tout[v] − tin[v] is convention-dependent — mixing inclusive/exclusive tout with the wrong sz formula breaks ranges.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Warns to pick one tin/tout/sz convention and keep it consistent.

must_hit.point: Ancestor formulas tin[u]≤tin[v]&&tout[v]≤tout[u] vs tin[u]≤tin[v]≤tout[u] only match under the same tout convention.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Refuses to mix the two ancestor forms across incompatible tout conventions.

must_hit.point: Forgetting −δ at tout[v]+1 (or the matching range-add end) corrupts root→node prefix answers after updates.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Calls out the missing difference endpoint on path-to-root updates.

must_hit.point: Using Euler alone for arbitrary path aggregates with updates — usually need HLD (Path Queries II).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects Euler-only for update+arbitrary-path aggregates and names HLD.

must_hit.point: On u–v paths, omitting path(u)+path(v)−2·path(lca) (edges) or the ±value[lca] node-weight adjustment double-counts or drops the LCA.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Requires the LCA term for edge vs node path reconstruction.

probes: What breaks if your tout convention and sz formula disagree?
What goes wrong if you skip the −δ at tout+1 on a path-to-root update?
When is Euler the wrong tool versus HLD?

hints.1: Check timestamp conventions, difference endpoints, LCA terms, and whether the path is arbitrary under updates.
hints.2: Stick to one tin/tout/sz convention; pair ancestor forms with that convention; always close the diff with −δ at tout+1; add LCA for u–v; HLD when Euler can’t do arbitrary path aggregates with updates.
hints.3: Say: sz=tout−tin is convention-dependent; don’t mix ancestor inequalities across tout styles; path-to-root needs +δ at tin and −δ at tout+1; u–v needs path(u)+path(v)−2·path(lca) or ±value[lca]; arbitrary path aggregates with updates → HLD / Path Queries II.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: Euler shines for subtrees and root-paths (flatten + BIT/segtree). Arbitrary path aggregates with updates usually need HLD (Path Queries II).
Subtree PURS: store at tin[v], point update, range query [tin[v], tout[v]]. Path root→u: range-add [tin[v], tout[v]] by δ via BIT-as-diff (+δ at tin[v], −δ at tout[v]+1), answer = prefix to tin[u].

tradeoffs.topic: Fenwick/segtree PURS vs lazy segtree on the tour
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Point-set / range-sum (or min/OR) on subtrees → Fenwick or plain segtree. Subtree assign / flip → lazy segtree on the tour array (Danil / New Year Tree / Water Tree).

tradeoffs.topic: Offline last-occurrence BIT vs small-to-large for distinct colors
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Offline distinct-in-subtree: scan Euler order, keep only last index of each color in a BIT (Distinct Colors). Alternative: small-to-large.

gotchas.trap: Mixing tin/tout conventions with sz[v] = tout[v] − tin[v] so subtree ranges are off-by-one.
gotchas.correction: Pick one tin/tout (in/out) convention and stick to it; sz[v] = tout[v] − tin[v] is convention-dependent.

gotchas.trap: Using one ancestor inequality with a tout style that matches the other form.
gotchas.correction: Use tin[u] ≤ tin[v] && tout[v] ≤ tout[u], or equivalently tin[u] ≤ tin[v] ≤ tout[u] only with a matching tout convention.

gotchas.trap: Updating a node for path-to-root sums without the −δ at tout[v]+1 difference end.
gotchas.correction: On value change of v by δ: +δ at tin[v], −δ at tout[v]+1 (range-add [tin[v], tout[v]]); answer is prefix sum to tin[u].

gotchas.trap: Reaching for Euler alone on arbitrary path aggregates with updates.
gotchas.correction: Euler shines for subtrees and root-paths; arbitrary path aggregates with updates usually need HLD (Path Queries II).

gotchas.trap: Building u–v path from root prefixes without the LCA correction.
gotchas.correction: path(u)+path(v)−2·path(lca) for edge weights, or adjust by ±value[lca] for node weights; need an LCA template.
